title: Utility Line Protection Plans: Wall and Ceiling Restoration Rates After an Interior Reroute
content:
# Wall and Ceiling Restoration Rates After an Interior Reroute

Restoration rate card, Bridgewell Utility Line Protection Plans, interior supply and drain lines. The rate is sized from the living area on the household's Homeowner Service Contracts record.

## Rule

A rerouted line is run through walls and ceilings, and the drywall opened for it grows with the size of the home; drywall is not one of the restoration allowances the base rule pays inside the occurrence cap, and Bridgewell sizes it from the living area on its own records, so a home with no living area on those records is restored at the standard size. Interior wall restoration: on an interior line that calls for whole-line work, a home whose living area recorded on the household's active Bridgewell homeowner service contract for the same property address is at least the large-home area in square feet adds the large-home wall restoration, and a home recorded below the large-home area in square feet, or with no living area recorded on such a contract, adds the standard wall restoration; every other request adds no wall restoration. The interior wall restoration is paid on top of the occurrence cap, and only for permanent interior work whose contractor quote is above the interior permanent-work payment.

An interior line calls for whole-line work when the plan replaces whole lines after repeat breaks, which is when its full replacement break count is above zero, and the most recent completed repair on the same line was completed no more than the plan's replacement lookback days before the request date.

## Plan figures that decide whole-line work

| Plan covering interior lines | Full-replacement break count | Replacement lookback |
|---|---|---|
| Bridgewell Interior Plumbing and Drainage Plan | 0 (the plan does not replace whole lines after repeat breaks) | 0 days |
| Bridgewell Total Home Lines Plan | 2 | 730 days |

## Rates

| Calls for whole-line work | Living area on an active Homeowner Service Contracts contract of the household at the same property address | Interior wall restoration |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 2000 square feet or more (large-home area: 2000) | $450.00 (large-home wall restoration) |
| yes | below 2000 square feet | $300.00 (standard wall restoration) |
| yes | no such active contract, or no living area recorded on it | $300.00 (standard wall restoration) |
| no | any | none |

## Records read

- From the household's Homeowner Service Contracts: the contract's status (it must be active), its property address (it must be the address of the line plan) and the living area recorded on it.
- From the line plan's claim history: the most recent completed repair on the same line and its completion date.

## Boundary cases

- Living area recorded as exactly 2000 square feet: $450.00. Recorded as 1999: $300.00.
- A homeowner service contract for a different address, or one that is not active, does not count; the standard rate applies.
